sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **District Administration (जिला प्रशासन)** is the foundational unit of public administration, law enforcement, and revenue collection in India.
Institutionalized systematically under British rule via the **Indian Councils Act 1861** and the creation of the **District Collector** post in **1772** by **Warren Hastings**.
Operates across all states and union territories in India, with Uttar Pradesh having **75 districts** divided into administrative divisions.
Headed by the **District Magistrate (DM) / District Collector**, who belongs to the **Indian Administrative Service (IAS)**.
Acts as the principal pivot for **law and order**, **revenue administration**, **disaster management**, and **electoral execution** at the grassroots level.
Dual role of the **Collector** (revenue) and **District Magistrate** (magisterial/police coordination); supervision of **Tehsils**, **Blocks**, and **Villages**.
High-scoring direct questions on **administrative hierarchy**, **revenue courts**, **panchayati raj integration**, and **Uttar Pradesh specific district data**.
UP has **18 administrative divisions**, **75 districts**, **351 tehsils**, and **826 development blocks**.

items.title: 1. Evolution and Historical Background
items.content:
• Post created in **1772** by **Governor-General Warren Hastings** as **Collector**.
• Initially, the focus was solely on **revenue collection** and civil justice.
• Lord Cornwallis separated revenue administration from judicial administration.
• Later, magisterial powers were added, converting the Collector into the **District Magistrate**.
• **Mnemonic for British Pioneers:** **'W-C-L'** (Warren Hastings created Collector, Lord Cornwallis separated Judiciary, Lytton expanded local bodies).

items.title: 2. Roles and Functions of the District Magistrate (DM)
items.content:
• **Head of Revenue Administration:** Manages land revenue, land reforms, record maintenance, and relief work.
• **District Collector:** Recovery of government dues, issuance of certificates (domicile, caste, income).
• **District Magistrate (Law & Order):** Controls police administration, executes **CrPC (Criminal Procedure Code)**, issues arms licenses, and supervises jails.
• **District Election Officer:** Conducts Lok Sabha, Vidhan Sabha, and local body elections.
• **Crisis & Disaster Manager:** Head of **District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)**.

items.title: 3. Administrative Hierarchy of Uttar Pradesh
items.content:
• **Division (मंडल):** Headed by **Divisional Commissioner** (Senior IAS).
• **District (जिला):** Headed by **District Magistrate / Collector** (IAS).
• **Sub-Division (तहसील):** Headed by **Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM)**.
• **Block (विकास खंड):** Headed by **Block Development Officer (BDO)**.
• **Village (ग्राम):** Headed by **Gram Panchayat / Gram Pradhan** with **Lekhpal** for land records.
• **Mnemonic for Hierarchy:** **'D-D-S-B-V'** -> **D**ivision, **D**istrict, **S**ub-division, **B**lock, **V**illage.

items.title: 4. Revenue Department Structure in a District
items.content:
• **Collector / DM** sits at the apex of district revenue machinery.
• **Additional District Magistrate (Revenue) [ADM-R]** assists the DM.
• **Tehsildar:** In charge of a Tehsil, handles land disputes and revenue collection.
• **Naib Tehsildar:** Assists Tehsildar in administrative and judicial revenue tasks.
• **Revenue Inspector (कानूनगो):** Supervises a circle of villages and Lekhpals.
• **Lekhpal (लेखपाल):** Maintains village land records (Khasra and Khatauni).

items.title: 5. Panchayati Raj and District Administration Convergence
items.content:
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992** institutionalized three-tier Panchayati Raj.
• **Zila Parishad:** Apex rural local body at the district level.
• **Chief Development Officer (CDO):** Acts as the CEO of Zila Parishad and heads rural development.
• **Panchayat Samiti:** Operates at the intermediate **Block** level.
• **Gram Panchayat:** Operates at the grassroots **Village** level.

items.definition: Remember **'M-Z-T-B-G'** -> **M**andal (Division), **Z**ila (District), **T**ehsil, **B**lock, **G**ram (Village).
Remember **'C-A-T-N-K-L'** -> **C**ollector, **A**DM, **T**ehsildar, **Naib** Tehsildar, **K**anungo, **L**ekhpal.
Associate **'Hasting for Haste'** -> **Warren Hastings** created the post in **1772** in a haste to organize land revenue.
Remember **'243 to 243-O'** covers the entire gamut of rural local bodies connected to district administration.
Remember **'Khasra = Crops & Physical details'** (Starts with C sound), **'Khatauni = Khata (Account of ownership)'**.
Remember **'CDO drives Development'** -> **Chief Development Officer** is the administrative brain behind Zila Parishad schemes.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing DM and Divisional Commissioner
items.definition: Students often interchange their roles. **Divisional Commissioner** supervises multiple districts, whereas the **DM** is in charge of a single district.
**Khasra** is a plot-wise survey number document, while **Khatauni** is an account book showing ownership of land across multiple plots.

items.term: Mistake 3: Misidentifying the Creator of Collectorate
items.definition: Do not confuse Lord Cornwallis with Warren Hastings. **Warren Hastings** created the Collector post; Cornwallis reformed and separated judiciary.
The **Chief Development Officer (CDO)** is a civil servant (IAS), whereas the **Zila Parishad Chairperson** is an elected representative.
Remember that a **Tehsildar** is a revenue and executive officer for a Tehsil, not the entire district.
**Article 243G** relates to powers of Panchayats, while **Article 243ZD** relates to the **District Planning Committee (DPC)**.
**District Administration** is the backbone of governance, executing laws, collecting revenue, and maintaining public order.
The **District Magistrate (DM)** is the executive head, holding dual responsibilities as Collector and Magistrate.
Established in **1772** by **Warren Hastings** to streamline revenue collection under British colonial rule.
Uttar Pradesh has **75 districts**, **18 administrative divisions**, **351 tehsils**, and **826 development blocks**.
Comprises **ADM**, **Tehsildar**, **Naib Tehsildar**, **Kanungo**, and **Lekhpal** for land administration.
The DM commands police coordination under the **Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC)** to maintain peace.
The DM acts as the **District Election Officer** for conducting all major democratic elections.
Heads the **District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)** during floods, droughts, and pandemics.
Works alongside the **Zila Parishad** and **Chief Development Officer (CDO)** for rural welfare.
Maintains critical legal documents like **Khasra** and **Khatauni** for property rights.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize exact figures for UP districts (75), divisions (18), and tehsils (351) as direct factual questions are frequently asked.
Pay special attention to the difference between Khasra and Khatauni, as questions regarding land revenue vocabulary appear in almost every UP subordinate exam.
Trap: Questions often state that the Divisional Commissioner collects land revenue. Remember, land revenue collection is the primary duty of the District Collector/DM, not the Commissioner.
Trap: Students often confuse the role of the Block Development Officer (BDO) with the Tehsildar. BDO handles developmental schemes, whereas Tehsildar handles revenue and land records.

keyTakeaways: District Administration is headed by the **District Magistrate / Collector** (IAS cadre).
Uttar Pradesh consists of **75 districts** distributed across **18 divisions**.
The revenue hierarchy runs from **Collector** down to **Lekhpal**.
**Khasra** tracks physical plot details, while **Khatauni** tracks land ownership.
The **Chief Development Officer (CDO)** manages rural development at the district level.
